task.title: Decide whether a deleted task's own dependency edge can be removed
task.description:
A task's Blocks list can hold a row nobody can remove: a deleted task that still depends on this one. The edge is stored on the deleted task's own record, so removing it means mutating a tombstone, and the board shows the row as read-only rather than offering a control that would fail.

That is deliberate for now -- see the pull request for "Deleted dependencies break rendering and can't be removed", which fixed the layout defect and left this alone. The question this task carries is whether the edge should become removable, and it is a durable-format decision rather than a validation tweak.

FreeMutation refuses a tombstoned parent, and below it Apply refuses any non-restore pack against a tombstoned task as corrupt data, not as a validation error. That runs on every clone replaying history, not just on the writer.

set.remove is a generation 0 operation (see docs/architecture.md), the only generation that writes no reader marker. So a set.remove pack against a tombstoned task would be folded by every binary already in the wild, and every one of them would read that history as corrupt. Allowing it honestly means a new operation type in a new generation, so older clones fence themselves off, plus the architecture and reference docs.

docs/reference.md already models the case where origin tombstoned a task that a local operation still edits as a conflict to surface rather than something to permit, so permitting this would cut against the existing answer to the same situation.

The edge is inert while the task is deleted: readiness is computed from a task's own dependencies, and deleted tasks are skipped before dependencies are consulted at all. It is panel noise, not incorrect state.

There is a working path today, verified end to end with workbook validate --full clean afterwards: restore the deleted task, free the dependency, delete it again.

So the options are roughly: leave it read-only and say so clearly, which is what ships now; mint a new-generation detach operation that may edit exactly this field on a tombstone; or stop listing tombstoned tasks in Blocks at all, which loses information the panel exists to show. Worth deciding rather than rediscovering.
